findings.title: Lack of Input Validation for Array Size
findings.trigger: If n is very large or negative, it can lead to excessive memory allocation or insufficient memory allocation, potentially leading to out-of-memory errors or invalid memory accesses.
findings.assumptions: The size n of the array is controlled by the caller of the countingSort function. There are no checks to ensure that n is within a reasonable range.

findings.title: Integer Overflow in Maximum Element Calculation
findings.trigger: If the array contains very large or negative values, the calculation of max can overflow, leading to incorrect behavior in the counting sort.
findings.assumptions: The array elements are untrusted and can have any integer value. There are no checks to prevent overflow.

findings.title: Double Free
findings.trigger: If the countingSort function is called multiple times with the same array and size, the memory allocated for count and output can be freed multiple times, leading to a double free error.
findings.assumptions: The countingSort function is called with the same array and size multiple times. There are no checks to ensure that the memory is not freed multiple times.

findings.title: Use of Uninitialized Data
findings.trigger: If the array is empty (n is 0), the count and output arrays are not properly initialized or used, leading to undefined behavior.
findings.assumptions: The array can be empty. There are no checks to handle the case where n is 0.
